home.heroBody: Cromo is the collector-grade home for stickers, cards, and everything you chase. Track parallels down to the 1-of-1, match with traders who need exactly what you have, and complete the album.
home.feature1Body: Border parallels, Crumple foils, Extras, Coca-Cola subset, Swiss United Edition — Cromo knows every variant Panini ships, and tracks what you own across all of them.
home.feature2Body: Cromo automatically surfaces collectors whose dupes line up with your wantlist. Swap your repeats for the ones you're chasing — no DMs, no spreadsheets.
home.feature3Body: From 1-in-2 blue parallels to the unique Black 1-of-1, Cromo respects the chase. Rarity tiers are honoured visually — common slate, ultra-rare emerald, unique chrome.

wc2026.label: 2026 FIFA World Cup
wc2026.title: Panini Sticker Collection
wc2026.description: Your friendly collector's handbook — picking the right edition, decoding those rare borders, and tracking down the hardest pulls.

wc2026Guide.heroBody: Everything you need to know to chase the 2026 album — which edition to buy, what those fancy borders actually mean, what's tucked inside the 980 slots, and the best places to track down the rare stuff.

editions.heading: Which edition should you buy?
editions.intro: Panini makes the same 980-sticker album for the whole world, but they dress it up a bit differently depending on where you live — a different cover, your local language, and sometimes a few exclusive stickers you can't get anywhere else. If you're chasing a specific rare border, it really does matter which version of the packs you buy.
editions.rowNaTraits: White-bordered stickers; six border parallels (Blue, Red, Purple, Green, Black, Orange)
editions.rowIntlTraits: No white border on stickers; 20 bonus elite-player stickers in Purple / Bronze / Silver / Gold (no album slot — collectibles only)
editions.rowChTraits: Thicker paper; metallised softcover; exclusive Green parallel stickers; numbered Treasure Box hardcover (1–5000)
editions.rowBeTraits: Silver parallel (players only) exclusive to Special Blister packs
editions.rowOtherRegion: Brazil, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Colombia, and more
editions.rowOtherTraits: Same base content; regional cover art; France also has Silver and Gold premium hardcover editions
editions.footnote: The team pages aren't in the same order in every album — your home country usually gets a spot near the front. North American albums lead with Canada, Mexico, and the USA; LATAM editions put Brazil and Argentina up first.

formats.heading: Softcover, hardcover & beyond
formats.intro: The album comes in a few different flavours depending on where you shop. The stickers inside are always the same 980 — what changes is the cover (paperback, hardcover, fancy metallic) and how easy it is to actually find.
formats.hardAvail: Global — Amazon Collectors Bundle and select retailers
formats.platinumWarning: Heads up: there's no such thing as a "Platinum" edition. If you see one listed online, it's a fake — don't pay extra for it.

variants.heading: The fancy sticker variants
variants.matteDesc: — your everyday stickers. Most of what you'll pull will be these.
variants.foilDesc: — the eye-catching ones. There are 49 in total: the "We Are Panini" sticker
variants.foilDescTail: , the eight World Cup branding stickers (FWC-1 to FWC-8), and the team emblem for each of the 48 nations.
variants.bordersIntro: If you buy packs in the US or Canada, you'll occasionally get stickers with coloured borders instead of plain white. The rarer the colour, the bigger the brag. Foil stickers always come with the regular border — they don't get the colour treatment.
variants.crumpleIntro: These are the wrinkled metallic ones — a totally separate line you can only get through Panini America's iCollect online store. You won't find them in any physical pack from a shop.
variants.belgiumDesc: — Belgium-exclusive, hidden inside the Special Blister packs
variants.extrasBody: International packs sometimes throw in a bonus sticker of one of 20 superstars in Purple, Bronze, Silver, or Gold — about once every 100 packs. They're fun to pull, but they don't go in the album. Think of them as a side collection.

breakdown.heading: What's actually in the album
breakdown.intro: Every album has the same 980 spots to fill, laid out across 112 pages. Here's how they break down:
breakdown.brandingNotes: Emblem ×2, Mascot, Slogan, Ball — all Foil
breakdown.hostsNotes: Canada, Mexico, USA emblems — all Foil
breakdown.champsNotes: Team photos of past World Cup winners (back of album). Some champions (e.g. Italy '38, Brazil '58, England '66) are printed directly in the album and are not collectible sticker slots.
breakdown.teamsNotes: Per team: 1 Foil emblem + 18 player stickers + 1 team photo
breakdown.ccNotes: Double-page spread in the middle of the album. Not in standard packs — see section 5.

cocaCola.heading: The Coca-Cola section
cocaCola.intro1: In the middle of every album there's a special two-page spread for stickers
cocaCola.intro3: — a Panini × Coca-Cola crossover featuring some of the tournament's biggest names. The slots are the same everywhere, but who fills them depends on which corner of the world your packs come from. Some slots even change player by region — CC9 alone has Davies in North America, Saliba in Europe, and Ayew in the Rest of World.

whereToBuy.heading: Where to grab some packs
whereToBuy.supermarketsDesc: The easiest place to start. Walmart, Target, Tesco, Carrefour — you'll find the regular softcover album and loose packs (about 5 stickers a pack) right next to the checkout.
whereToBuy.amazonDesc: The Collectors Bundle comes with a hardcover album. In the US and Canada you can also grab the Amazon-exclusive box of packs — that's where the orange-border stickers live.
whereToBuy.paniniDesc: paniniamerica.net, panini.co.uk, panini.de, and so on. Good for starter packs, blister packs, bigger bundles, and country-specific goodies.
whereToBuy.hobbyDesc: If you want to go big, these shops carry full boxes and premium bundles. They're also where you'll find live box-break events and the harder-to-pull stuff.
whereToBuy.swissDesc: Sold through Swiss Panini sellers and panini.ch. The numbered Treasure Box hardcover (only 5,000 made) is exclusive to here.
whereToBuy.franceDesc: Check Fnac, Leclerc, or the Panini France online store.
whereToBuy.icollectDesc: Digital-only packs at icollect.paniniamerica.net. This is the only place to get those Crumple stickers — nothing ships to your door.
whereToBuy.appDesc: The official companion app. Handy for keeping tabs on what you've collected and seeing the album layout for your region.
whereToBuy.ebayDesc: Where most collectors buy and sell singles, sealed packs, and rare borders. Prices are all over the map — shop around before you commit.
whereToBuy.priceFootnote: Prices and stock listed above are rough as of May 2026 — they bounce around a lot between countries and shops. And remember: page numbers shift between regional editions, so if you're looking for a specific spot, the table of contents in your own album (or the FIFA Panini Collection app) is your best friend.
